serialFormats.description: 10-character Lennox serial (1973 to present): 2-digit plant/factory code, 2-digit year, 1 month letter (A-M skipping I), 5-digit production sequence. Used on residential and commercial equipment alike.
sources: Building Intelligence Center, 'Lennox HVAC age' (building-center.org/lennox-hvac-age/) - style 1 examples 1606B13871 (Feb 2006) and 5899L17212; positions 1-2 plant, 3-4 year, 5 month letter
PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - month letters A-M skipping I; 5806E12345 = plant 58, May 2006
Parts Town, 'Lennox Serial Number Lookup' (partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/lennox-serial-number-lookup) - plant code list 51/53/54/55/56/58/63
hvacdecoder.com Lennox serial number decoder - agrees on plant/year/month-letter layout
notes: Year = characters 3-4 (two digits). Pivot 70: 73-99 -> 1973-1999, 00-69 -> 2000s. The format has been in continuous use since 1973 so a two-digit year is unambiguous within the era.
Month letter skips I: A=Jan ... H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec. A serial with I or N-Z in position 5 is not this format (re-read the plate).

Plant map covers only the codes documented by the secondary sources (51/53/54/55/56/58/63, confirmed by thedailythrive.org and furnace.direct / Parts Town; one lists 55 as 'Heatcraft', consistent with Stone Mountain, GA). Observed but unmapped plant codes: 16 (building-center example 1606B13871) and 52 (InspectorHandbook example 5207K24862 = Oct 2007) - the decoder reports the raw code. Unknown plant codes still decode (year/month).

Confidence is medium (three independent secondary decoders agree); Lennox's own 'Model and Serial Nomenclature' PDF (lennox.com/lib/legacy-res/pdfs/lennox_model_and_serial_nomenclature.pdf) is the primary source but could not be read in this session - promote to high once a warranty lookup on LennoxPros (Resources > Warranty lookup by serial) confirms three dated examples.
Residential and commercial Lennox units share this serial style; the difference is only the plant code (commercial rooftops are typically 56 Stuttgart AR or 58 Marshalltown IA).
Cross-check: the compressor date code and the refrigerant printed on the nameplate (R-22 before ~2008-2010 on rooftops, R-410A after, R-454B from 2025) should agree with the decoded year.

serialFormats.description: 9-character Lennox serial reported for the late 1970s to early 1990s: a letter, five digits, three letters; characters 2-3 are the year, the second-to-last character is the month letter.
sources: PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - 'Style #2': letter + 5 numbers + 3 letters, 2nd/3rd characters = year (86 = 1986), second-to-last letter = month (D = April)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only one secondary source (PickHVAC) describes this style, and Building Intelligence Center states the 10-character plant/year/month style has been used exclusively since 1973 - the two sources disagree on whether this style exists. Treat any decode as a hint and confirm the year from the nameplate style and refrigerant (R-22 era).
The two examples are CONSTRUCTED to exercise the published rule; they are not real nameplates. Replace with dated nameplate photos when available.
The month-letter map (A-M skipping I) is assumed to match the 1973+ style; PickHVAC only confirms D = April.
No collision with the 10-character style: this style starts with a letter and is 9 characters long; the 1973+ style is all digits except position 5.

Only PickHVAC describes this style; Building Intelligence Center says the 10-character style has been exclusive since 1973 - when a serial matches both styles, prefer the 10-character decode. No second independent source was found in a verification pass of eight serial-related searches (a search-summary sample C89274AAC decodes to 1989-01 under this rule).

modelFormats.family: Energence LGH/LCH packaged rooftop (3-50 ton; gas/electric and electric/electric)
modelFormats.description: Lennox Energence rooftop units (2009-2024, R-410A). Letters: L = Lennox, G/C = unit type, H = major design sequence (Energence generation), 3-digit nominal cooling MBH, cooling efficiency letter, refrigerant digit (4 = R-410A), blower type letter, heat-input letter, minor design digit, voltage letter, optional factory feature suffix.

segments.name: Nominal cooling capacity (MBH)
segments.notes: Lennox uses 074 for the 6-ton high-efficiency size and 092 for the 7.5-ton high-efficiency size (Raider nomenclature confirms 072 and 074 = 6 tons); all other codes are MBH/12 (036 = 3, 120 = 10, 150 = 12.5).

segments.name: Cooling efficiency
segments.notes: S/H/U confirmed by Lennox LGH service literature (036U-074U ultra, 036H-060H high). Map may not cover every published code.

segments.name: Blower type
segments.notes: B (belt CAV) and E (direct-drive MSAV) confirmed from LennoxPros catalog titles for LGH120H4BH and LGH036H4ES; M (belt MSAV) from the LGH120H4B/M listing; D is unconfirmed (verify on the Lennox rooftop model number identifier sheet 38Z29). T (belt MSAV) and V (belt VAV) added from the Lennox LGH 20-50 ton EHB (ehb_lgh_dbox_2309 / ehb_lgh_ebox_1906: M = MSAV belt, V = VAV belt) and LennoxPros BX337 (LGH074H4TH 'Belt Drive-MSAV'). The regex accepts any letter here; letters not in the map are reported raw.

segments.name: Heat input / factory heat
segments.notes: H = high heat confirmed by the LGH120H4BH catalog listing (240,000 Btuh input). S/M inferred from Lennox convention; N = no heat confirmed on Raider ZCA nomenclature. Electric-heat kW codes on LCH units are not mapped. On electric/electric LCH/LCT/LCX/LCM units the same position is the factory electric-heat kW code (LCH manual: N none, E 15 kW, J 30 kW, K 45 kW, L 60 kW, P 90 kW, S 120 kW) and must not be read as gas heat - the map below applies to gas/electric (G) units only. Unknown letters are reported as the raw code. P/R (modulating) from the Lennox LGH 20-50 ton EHB sheets (S = standard 2-stage, H = high 2-stage, P = standard modulating, R = high modulating). A trailing W on single-phase LennoxPros listings (LGH036H4EW, KGB036S4EW) lands in this position as the raw code W; its meaning is unconfirmed.

segments.name: Minor design sequence
segments.notes: 1 = 1st revision, 2 = 2nd, 3 = 3rd (per Raider ZCA nomenclature sheet; same Lennox convention).

segments.name: Voltage
segments.notes: Voltage letters confirmed on the Raider ZCA/ZCB nomenclature sheet and LennoxPros listings (Y = 208-230 V 3 ph, G = 460 V 3 ph). 50 Hz export codes are not mapped. LennoxPros single-phase listings also end in W (LGH036H4EW, KGB036S4EW); whether W is a voltage code or a single-phase heat variant is unconfirmed - read the nameplate volts. W is not mapped until the 38Z29 identifier sheet is read.

notes: Nameplate: the factory model number is on the unit rating plate ('MODEL NO.') on the compressor/control-compartment side; it is the full string (e.g. LGH120H4BH1G) possibly followed by factory-option characters. LennoxPros catalog/stock numbers (L1318, 45W08 ...) are sales numbers, not model numbers - never decode those.
Service literature and engineering handbooks abbreviate the model (LGH120H4B, LGH036H4ES); the decoder accepts these partial strings.

Examples LGH120H4BH1G and LGH036H4ES1Y extend confirmed partial catalog strings (LGH120H4BH 460 V; LGH036H4ES 208-230 V 3 ph) with the minor-design digit and voltage letter; LCH150H4BN1G is constructed from the nomenclature. Verify against a real nameplate before relying on the last two positions.

Energence units shipped with the Prodigy (M2) unit controller from 2009, Prodigy 2.0 (M3) from ~2013, and Lennox CORE (M4) on later production; check the controller label (A55) inside the control compartment.
Sizes 036-300 = 3-25 tons; larger Energence (13-50 ton) use the same string with codes 156-600.
LCH072H4BJ3Y is a real listing (6 ton, 30 kW electric heat, 208/230 V 3 ph): the J in the heat position is the electric-heat kW code, reported raw because this map covers gas heat only.
sources: Lennox LGH Series Service Literature, Corp. 0924-L11 (3-6 ton) and Corp. 1605-L11 - unit information and model nomenclature (lennox.com/dA/08178a7baa/0924e.pdf, lennox.com/dA/e60652ca18/1605.pdf)

LennoxPros catalog listings LGH120H4BH (10 ton, high efficiency, 240,000 Btuh, belt drive-CAV, 460 V 3 ph) and LGH036H4ES (3 ton, direct drive-MSAV, 208-230 V 3 ph)
Lennox Raider ZCA/ZCB installation instructions nomenclature (device.report) - voltage letters P/Y/G/J, refrigerant 4 = R-410A, minor design 1/2/3, N = no heat, blower B/T
Lennox Rooftop Model Number Identifier Sheet 38Z29 (lennox.com/dA/4463733165/38Z29_Rooftop+Model+Number+Identifier+Sheet_LR.pdf) - referenced, not read in this session
Lennox LGH 20-50 ton Engineering Handbooks (tech.lennoxintl.com ehb_lgh_dbox_2309.pdf, ehb_lgh_ebox_1906.pdf) - blower M = MSAV belt, V = VAV belt; heat S/H 2-stage, P/R modulating

controls.name: Lennox Prodigy (M2) / Prodigy 2.0 (M3) unit controller
controls.description: Microprocessor unit controller with LCD and push-button menu fitted to Energence (and late Strategos) rooftops: Prodigy M2 (2009-2013, setup guide 506215-01 / application guide 506457) and Prodigy 2.0 M3 (2013+, setup guide 507241-07, application guide 507242-07). Alarm/event codes are numeric; selected alarms close the service relay contacts (DO1). Coverage is partial: roughly 100 of the Prodigy 2.0 Table 65 rows were transcribed through search excerpts of the guide (see the coverage note in diagnosticTips for the rows still missing and the rows whose display text is reconstructed). The application guide narrative and Table 65 disagree on alarm 60 (narrative: gas valve cycled on heat section 2; table: heat section 2 primary limit S99, with 69 as the heat-2 gas-valve strike) - table numbering is used here. Prodigy M2 uses the same numbering for the common codes (2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 20, 74, 93 confirmed) plus its own controller-hardware codes 112, 114 and 118, which are reserved on the M3.

faultCodes.meaning: Blower alarm (S52 blower airflow proving) - repeated code 5 alarms result in the 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER' lockout.
likelyCauses: Blower not proving airflow (broken/slipping belt, blower motor or VFD fault, S52 airflow switch or its tubing)
Dirty filters / closed dampers starving the blower
checks: Confirm blower rotation and belt condition; check motor amps against nameplate FLA
Verify S52 airflow switch closes on blower start (check tubing and switch setpoint)
Check blower motor overload / VFD status
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 (M3 Unit Controller) Application Guide 507242, Table 65 'Prodigy 2.0 Alarm and Event Codes' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.147-156)
faultCodes.notes: Meaning paraphrased from the guide's 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER' entry, which references multiple alarm code 5 events; verify the exact wording in Table 65.

faultCodes.meaning: Lockout is active - multiple alarm code 5 (blower) events detected. Can be manually cleared through the user interface.
likelyCauses: Repeated blower proving failures (see code 5)
checks: Fix the underlying blower/airflow fault, then clear the lockout from the controller UI (Service menu)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 (M3 Unit Controller) Application Guide 507242, Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298)

faultCodes.meaning: RESET CONTROLLER - Check unit settings; contact Lennox if problem persists.
likelyCauses: Controller reset / watchdog restart (power glitch, firmware fault)
Corrupt or conflicting unit configuration
checks: Verify unit configuration ID and parameters after the reset (Settings > Install)
Check incoming power quality and 24 VAC transformer output (field practice)
If it repeats, record alarm history and call Lennox technical support
faultCodes.source: Prodigy M2 Installation & Setup Guide 506215-01 Event Codes ('CODE 2: RESET CONTROLLER, CHECK UNIT SETTINGS, CONTACT LENNOX IF PROBLEM PERSISTS'); code also listed in Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: SMOKE MODE - Check for source of smoke. While the Smoke Alarm is active the M3 unit controller will not service any cooling, heating or ventilation demands.
likelyCauses: Smoke detector A171/A172 tripped or in fault
Smoke-detector wiring open / detector needs reset
checks: Locate and clear the source of smoke before resetting
Reset the smoke detector(s) A171/A172 and verify the input returns to normal
Smoke-mode blower/damper/exhaust behaviour is set by parameter 109
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.147-156) and Prodigy M2 guide 506215-01 ('CODE 4: SMOKE MODE, CHECK FOR SOURCE OF SMOKE')

faultCodes.meaning: DIRTY FILTER S27 - Replace filter or check filter switch S27. Alarm clears automatically once the switch is detected open.
likelyCauses: Dirty filters (S27 closes on high filter pressure drop)
Mis-set or failed dirty-filter switch or its tubing
checks: Replace filters
If filters are clean, check S27 setpoint and sensing tubing; S27 is open during normal operation
Service alarm output (if configured) turns on with this code
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and 'Dirty Filter Switch (S27)' section (ManualsLib 1251298 p.20); Prodigy M2 guide 506215-01 ('CODE 6: REPLACE FILTER OR CHECK FILTER SWITCH S27')

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER S52 - Lockout, multiple code 5 (air flow switch) events; check blower parts. Can be manually cleared through the user interface.
likelyCauses: Repeated air-flow proving failures (belt, blower motor/VFD, S52 switch or tubing)
checks: Correct the underlying code 5 cause, then clear the lockout from the Service menu
Number of strikes is 3 by default (parameter 43)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 ('STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER S52'); Prodigy M2 guide 506215-01 ('CODE 8: LOCKOUT, MULTIPLE CODE 5, CHECK BLOWER PARTS')
faultCodes.notes: Same alarm as the existing text entry 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER'; this is its numeric code.

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 1 HIGH PRESS S4 - Compressor is off. Check charge, fans, coil.
likelyCauses: Dirty/blocked condenser coil or failed condenser fan
Overcharge or non-condensables
On some compressors a high-temperature switch is in series with S4, so a high-temperature trip also gives this code
checks: Check condenser fan operation and coil cleanliness
Check charge (subcooling) and head pressure
Compressor restarts only after S4 closes and the minimum off delay expires; 3 trips in one demand (parameter 98) locks out (code 13)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.138 / 1251298 p.153)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ON COMP 1 HIGH PRESS S4 - Compressor lockout. Check charge, fans, coil. Use service menu to clear lockouts.
likelyCauses: Three high-pressure (or high-temperature) trips in a single demand cycle
checks: Fix the cause of code 12, then clear the lockout via Service > Lockouts
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.138)

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 2 HIGH PRESS S7 - Compressor is off. Check charge, fans, coil.
likelyCauses: Condenser airflow problem, overcharge, non-condensables, or high-temperature switch S8 trip (in series on some units)
checks: As for code 12, on circuit/compressor 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.138)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ON COMP 2 HIGH PRESS S7 - Compressor lockout. Use service menu to clear lockouts.

faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.138)

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 3 HIGH PRESS S28 - Compressor is off. Check charge, fans and coil.

faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.153)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ON COMP 3 HIGH PRESS S28 - Compressor lockout (three high-pressure/high-temperature trips in one demand cycle).

checks: Fix the cause of code 16, then clear the lockout via the Service menu

checks: As for code 12, on compressor 4

faultCodes.meaning: PHASE MONITOR (A42) - Unit shutdown; check phase monitor. Alarm is set if the installed phase monitor (A42) is detected open and clears automatically when A42 is detected closed.
likelyCauses: Phase loss, phase reversal, or voltage imbalance tripping the external phase monitor A42
A42 wiring/configuration on DI-2 or DI-3 wrong (Config ID 2 position 5)
checks: Check incoming three-phase voltage and phase rotation
Check the A42 monitor's LED/status and its output to DI-2/DI-3
If A42 is not fitted, set the phase/voltage detection option to Not Installed or Internal

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 1 LOW PRESS S87 - Compressor de-energized due to open low pressure switch S87 (five-minute off, default).
likelyCauses: Low charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow (filters, belt, dampers) or low outdoor ambient
Restriction (TXV, filter drier); switch trips more readily at low outdoor temperatures
checks: Check suction pressure and superheat; look for leaks
Check airflow and filters

checks: Fix the cause of code 36, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 4 FRZSTAT OPEN S95 - Compressor is off. Check freezestat, air flow, charge, coil, air filter and outside air temperature.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, low charge, low ambient, or faulty S95
checks: As for code 32, on compressor 4
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 COMP 4 FRZSTAT OPEN S95 - Compressor lockout.
likelyCauses: Three S95 trips in one demand cycle
checks: Fix the cause of code 38, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: RETURN AIR OVER HEAT LIMIT RT16 - Heat is above set point. Check space conditions and sensors. (Displayed but not stored in memory for recall.)
likelyCauses: Return air temperature above the heat return-air limit (parameter 115) - heating demand is interrupted
Faulty RT16 return air sensor or thermostat calling for heat with a warm space
checks: Verify space and return-air temperature against the limit
Check RT16 resistance/wiring
Review parameter 115 (heat return air limit)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150) and 'Return Air Temperature Limits' text ('Codes 40 or 41 are displayed but not stored in memory for recall')
faultCodes.notes: Display label reconstructed from the alarm 41 wording ('RETURN AIR UNDER COOL LIMIT RT16'); the action text is verbatim.

faultCodes.meaning: RETURN AIR UNDER COOL LIMIT RT16 - Cool below setpoint. Check space conditions or sensor. (Displayed but not stored in memory for recall.)
likelyCauses: Return air temperature below the cool return-air limit (parameter 114) - cooling demand is interrupted
Faulty RT16 sensor or thermostat calling for cooling in a cold space
checks: Verify return-air temperature; check RT16 and wiring
Review parameter 114 (cool return air limit)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: UNIT SHUTDOWN S42 OR S135 - Check 2 amp fuse; check external motor overloads.
likelyCauses: Blower overload relay S42 (or S135) tripped
Blown 2 A control fuse
Motor overload / high amps, wrong VFD settings
checks: Check the 2 amp fuse on the control board
Check blower motor amps vs FLA, belt tension, and the overload setting
Reset the overload; three occurrences give code 43
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 UNIT SHUTDOWN S42 OR S135 - Check external motor overloads.
likelyCauses: Repeated S42/S135 overload trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 42, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: GAS VALVE ON NO DEMAND GV1 - Unit off. Check gas pressure, gas valve. (M2 wording: 'GV1 POWER BUT NO DEMAND'.)
likelyCauses: Gas valve GV1 sensed energized with no heating demand (welded relay, miswire, ignition control fault)
checks: Check for 24 VAC at GV1 with no W1 demand; check ignition control A3 and gas valve wiring
Check manifold and supply gas pressure
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150); Prodigy M2 guide Table 8

faultCodes.meaning: GAS VALVE ON NO DEMAND GV3 - Unit off. Check gas pressure, gas valve.
likelyCauses: Gas valve GV3 (heat section 2) sensed energized with no demand
checks: As for code 44, on heat section 2 / GV3
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: PRIMARY HEAT 1 LIMIT OPEN S10 - Heat section 1 primary gas heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, air filter, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow across the heat exchanger (filters, belt, blower speed, closed dampers)
Over-fired burner / high gas pressure
Failed or miswired S10 limit
checks: Check airflow, filters and blower
Check temperature rise and manifold pressure
Gas valve is de-energized and blower energized; three opens in a thermostat cycle lock out the heat section for one hour (code 51)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 50-51, ManualsLib 1251298 p.150) and 'Primary or Secondary Limits (S10 and S99)' section

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 PRIMARY HEAT 1 LIMIT OPEN S10 - Heat section 1 locked out (one hour) after the primary limit opened three times in a thermostat cycle. Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Repeated S10 limit trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 50, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 50-51)

faultCodes.meaning: SECONDARY HEAT 1 LIMIT OPEN S21 - Heat section 1 secondary gas heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, air filter, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, over-firing, or failed S21 secondary limit
checks: As for code 50; also check the secondary limit S21 location and wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 52-53, ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 SECONDARY HEAT 1 LIMIT OPEN S21 - Heat section 1 locked out after the secondary limit opened three times.
likelyCauses: Repeated S21 trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 52, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 52-53)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 1 ROLLOUT OPEN S47 - Heat section 1 flame roll out burner 1 switch is open. Check gas roll out switch S47 and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout (blocked heat exchanger / flue, cracked heat exchanger, poor combustion air)
Tripped manual-reset rollout switch S47
checks: Find the cause of rollout before resetting: inspect heat exchanger, flue and burners
Gas valve is de-energized; S47 requires a manual reset
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 54-55 heat section 1, 'Heat section 1 flame roll out burner 1 switch is open. Check gas roll out switch S47'; parallel entry 64 'HEAT 2 ROLLOUT OPEN S69')
faultCodes.notes: Display wording reconstructed from the documented row pattern, not seen verbatim in a Table 65 excerpt - verify against Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 pp.153-156 / 507242-07). One summary of Table 65 rendered rows 54-55 as 'HEAT 1 LIMIT OPEN'; the row text seen is the roll-out description. Verify the exact display label.

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 ROLLOUT OPEN S47 - Heat section 1 locked out after repeated roll-out switch opens. Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated rollout trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 54, reset S47, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 54-55; parallel entry 65 'STRIKE 3 ROLLOUT OPEN S69')
faultCodes.notes: Display wording reconstructed from the documented row pattern, not seen verbatim in a Table 65 excerpt - verify against Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 pp.153-156 / 507242-07). Label inferred from the heat-2 pair 64/65; verify exact wording.

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18 - Check heat section 1 combustion air motor and proof switch. Set if S18 is not sensed closed within 30 seconds of energizing the combustion air inducer (closed-proof alarm).
likelyCauses: Combustion air inducer not running or weak (motor, capacitor, wiring)
Blocked flue / inlet, cracked or plugged pressure-switch tubing
Failed S18 proof switch
checks: Confirm the inducer runs on a heat call and check its amps
Check S18 tubing and switch make/break
Check flue and combustion air inlet for obstruction
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 56-57) and 'Combustion Air Inducer Proof Switch (S18 and S45)' section (ManualsLib 1593305 p.18)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18 - Heat section 1 locked out after three CAI proof-switch failures during a single demand. Check heat section 1 combustion air motor and proof switch.
likelyCauses: Repeated S18 proving failures
checks: Fix the cause of code 56, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.139 'ALARM STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18') and CAI section ('alarm(s) 57 and/or 67 when three-strikes occur during a single-demand')

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 1 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV1 - The M3 unit controller did not detect that the gas valve was energized within two minutes after a heating demand. Check ignition control, flame proof, GV1, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Ignition control A3 lockout (no flame / no spark)
Gas supply off or low pressure
Gas valve or its sensing feedback wiring open
checks: Watch the ignition control's status LED during a heat call
Verify gas supply and manifold pressure
Check GV1 feedback wiring to the M3
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 58-59) and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('error code 58 for gas heat section 1 and alarm 68 for gas heat section 2')

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV1 - Gas valve was energized and de-energized three times (default) during a single heating demand; heat section 1 locked out. Check ignition control, flame proof, GV1, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Flame loss / flame-sense problems (dirty flame rod, poor ground, low gas pressure)
Intermittent ignition control
checks: Check flame signal, flame rod and burner ground
Check gas pressure under load
Clear the lockout via the Service menu after repair
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('error code 59 for the gas heat section 1')

faultCodes.meaning: PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99 - Heat section 2 primary gas heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, air filter, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, over-firing, or failed S99 limit on heat section 2
checks: As for code 50, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (code 61 'STRIKE 3 PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99' implies 60 is the first-strike entry) and 'Primary or Secondary Limits (S10 and S99)' section
faultCodes.notes: The guide's gas-valve-sensing narrative also cites 'alarm 60 for gas heat section 2' for a cycled gas valve; Table 65 lists that condition as 69. Treat 60 as the heat 2 primary limit and verify against the table.

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99 - Check heat section 2 primary burner limit switch to see if it is open. Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Repeated S99 trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 60, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S100 - Heat section 2 secondary heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, over-firing, or failed S100 secondary limit
checks: As for code 52, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S100 - Heat section 2 secondary heat limit switch is open (three strikes). Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Repeated S100 trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 62, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 ROLLOUT OPEN S69 - Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout on heat section 2 (blocked flue/heat exchanger, combustion air)
Tripped manual-reset rollout switch S69
checks: Find the cause before resetting S69; inspect heat exchanger, flue and burners
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ROLLOUT OPEN S69 - Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated rollout trips on heat section 2
checks: Fix the cause of code 64, reset S69, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 CAI SWITCH S45 - Check heat section 2 combustion air motor and proof switch. Set if S45 is not sensed closed within 30 seconds of energizing the combustion air inducer.
likelyCauses: Inducer 2 not running, blocked flue/inlet, tubing, or failed S45
checks: As for code 56, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and CAI proof switch section ('Alarm 56 or 66')

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 2 CAI SWITCH S45 - Heat section 2 locked out after three CAI proof-switch failures in a single demand.
likelyCauses: Repeated S45 proving failures
checks: Fix the cause of code 66, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and CAI section ('alarm(s) 57 and/or 67')

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV3 - Gas valve for heat section 2 not detected energized within two minutes after a heating demand. Check heat section 2 ignition control, flame proof, gas valve and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Ignition control lockout on heat section 2, gas supply, or valve feedback wiring
checks: As for code 58, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 68-69) and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('alarm 68 for gas heat section 2')
faultCodes.notes: Heat section 2 valve is designated GV3 in Table 65 (codes 45 and 69); one summary labelled 68 as GV2.

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV3 HEAT SECT 2 - Check ignition control, flame proof, GV3, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated flame loss / gas valve cycling on heat section 2
checks: Fix the cause of code 68, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: NETWORK SENSOR ERROR - Check with integrator for refresh rate, network status lights and wiring. Alarm is removed when all BACnet network sensor inputs are received.
likelyCauses: BAS not writing a required network sensor value (zone temp, setpoint, etc.) within the refresh time
BACnet/LonTalk module or network wiring problem
checks: Confirm the BAS is writing every network sensor the configuration expects
Check module TX/RX LEDs and network wiring/termination
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150); M3 BACnet Module guide 1404

faultCodes.meaning: NO ZONE SENSOR - No zone sensor input; check zone sensor and wiring. (Backup sensor mode / code 93 follows if configured.)
likelyCauses: Unit configured for zone-sensor mode but wired for a thermostat
Open/shorted zone sensor A2 or its wiring
checks: Determine whether the unit should be in zone sensor or thermostat mode; setting it back to thermostat mode clears 74 and 93
Check A2 zone sensor resistance and wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65; Lennox Commercial Controls FAQ 507398 (codes 74/93)

faultCodes.meaning: OUTDOOR TEMP SENSOR RT17 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT17 outdoor air thermistor or wiring
checks: Measure RT17 resistance vs temperature (two-wire thermistor); check wiring and plug
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HUMIDITY SENSOR A91 - Check 2 amp fuse and sensor/wiring.
likelyCauses: Blown 2 A fuse feeding the sensor
Open/shorted humidity sensor A91 or wiring; sensor not installed but enabled
checks: Check the 2 amp fuse
Check A91 supply voltage and signal; verify the humidity-sensor configuration if no sensor is fitted
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: DISCHARGE AIR TEMP SENSOR RT6 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT6 discharge air thermistor (located in the discharge air just beyond the heat exchanger, accessible through the blower compartment)
checks: Measure RT6 resistance and check wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: RETURN AIR TEMP SENSOR RT16 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT16 return air thermistor or wiring
checks: Measure RT16 resistance and check wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: ADD-ON BOARD PROBLEM - Check add-on board and reset to clear.
likelyCauses: Add-on controller (e.g. C1/ECTO expansion, GP board) not communicating or failed
checks: Check add-on board connections and power; reset the controller to clear
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: REHEAT SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Humiditrol / supermarket reheat option configured without the required hardware or settings
checks: Review reheat (Humiditrol) settings in the unit configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROLLER RESET
likelyCauses: Controller restarted (power interruption, firmware watchdog)
checks: Check power quality; note frequency of resets in alarm history
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: INCORRECT SETTINGS
likelyCauses: Conflicting unit configuration ID / parameter settings
checks: Re-check the unit configuration ID against the nameplate and the setup guide
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: INCORRECT HUMIDITROL SETTINGS
likelyCauses: Humiditrol dehumidification configured inconsistently with the installed hardware
checks: Review the Humiditrol settings and dehumidification mode configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: CONFLICTING THERMOSTAT INPUT
likelyCauses: Simultaneous heating and cooling (Y and W) demands, or stage inputs present without the first stage
Thermostat wiring or thermostat fault
checks: Check thermostat inputs at the M3 (Y1/Y2/W1/W2/G) with a meter
Verify thermostat wiring and staging
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: BACKUP SENSOR MODE - Communication with the zone sensor was lost and the unit switched to the redundant back-up sensor (code broadcast over BACnet and shown on the Prodigy display). Check zone sensor and wiring; usually accompanies code 74.
likelyCauses: Zone sensor failure or wiring (see code 74)
Unit left in zone-sensor mode on a thermostat installation
checks: Fix the code 74 cause; change the unit back to thermostat mode if a thermostat is used
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65; Lennox Commercial Controls FAQ 507398; M3 BACnet Module guide 1404

faultCodes.meaning: MGV CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Modulating gas valve control option configured without the required settings/hardware
checks: Review the modulating gas heat configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: GP CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: General-purpose (GP) control add-on configured inconsistently
checks: Review GP board configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Advanced control option settings conflict
checks: Review advanced control settings in the configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: BUILDING PRESSURE SENSOR A34
likelyCauses: Building pressure sensor A34 signal out of range, missing, or wiring open
checks: Check A34 power, signal and tubing; verify the building pressure control option matches installed hardware
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: SUPPLY STATIC PRESSURE SENSOR ERROR (A30) - The Prodigy controller locks out unit operation after the Max Static Duct Pressure Occurrences have occurred.
likelyCauses: Duct static sensor A30 signal out of range, tubing disconnected, or wiring fault
checks: Check A30 supply voltage, output signal and sensing tubing
Verify the MSAV / VAV static-pressure configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH SUPPLY STATIC (DUCT) PRESSURE - Unit operation locked out after the Max Static Duct Pressure Occurrences.
likelyCauses: Closed VAV boxes / dampers, blocked ductwork, high-limit static setpoint too low
VFD not responding to the static-pressure control
checks: Check duct static against the high-limit setpoint; check VAV box operation and VFD control
Clear the lockout via the Service menu after correcting
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 DUCT SUPPLY PRESS SENSOR A30
likelyCauses: Repeated supply static sensor errors
checks: Fix the cause of code 107, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: WAITING ON NETWORK DATA
likelyCauses: Unit configured for network (BAS) control and required network values have not yet been received
checks: Confirm the BAS is writing the required points; check network wiring and module LEDs
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: PROFILE ERROR
likelyCauses: Unit profile / configuration data invalid
checks: Reload or verify the unit configuration; contact Lennox technical support if it persists
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: ADD-ON BOARD MCB PROBLEM
likelyCauses: Add-on control board communication or hardware fault
checks: Check add-on board connections; reset the controller
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: LINE FREQ DOES NOT MATCH UNIT CONFIG
likelyCauses: 50/60 Hz configuration does not match the measured line frequency
Poor power quality (generator) confusing the phase/voltage detection
checks: Verify the unit configuration frequency setting against the supply
Check power source quality
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC PRIMARY VOLTAGE LOW - Set when the calculated RMS 24 VAC is below the low-voltage alarm threshold (30 VAC per the guide's low-voltage text) for more than two seconds; the controller stops cooling, heating and ventilation.
likelyCauses: Low line voltage or wrong transformer primary tap
Overloaded / failing control transformer T1
High-resistance connections on the 24 VAC circuit
checks: Measure T1 secondary under load and line voltage at the unit
Check transformer tap selection for the supply voltage
Check 24 VAC wiring and connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155) and 'Phase-Voltage Detection' section (p.147)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC PRIMARY VOLTAGE HIGH - Calculated RMS 24 VAC above the high-voltage alarm threshold for more than two seconds.
likelyCauses: High line voltage or wrong transformer tap
checks: Measure T1 output and line voltage; correct the tap
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC SECONDARY VOLTAGE LOW
likelyCauses: Low secondary 24 VAC supply (second transformer/circuit) - overload, loose connection, transformer failing
checks: Measure the secondary 24 VAC circuit under load; check connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC SECONDARY VOLTAGE HIGH
likelyCauses: High secondary 24 VAC supply (line voltage / tap)
checks: Measure the secondary 24 VAC circuit; correct transformer tap
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: LINE PHASING DOES NOT MATCH UNIT CONFIG
likelyCauses: Phase rotation reversed (scroll compressors run backwards)
Single-phase/three-phase setting wrong in the configuration; DI-2 misconfigured when phase/voltage detection is enabled (unit goes to demand hold and restarts after 3 minutes)
checks: Check phase rotation with a meter and swap two incoming legs if reversed
Verify Config ID 2 position 5 (phase/voltage detection) and DI-2 settings
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155) and 'Phase-Voltage Detection' section

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC POWER LOSS
likelyCauses: Interruption of 24 VAC control power (transformer, fuse, disconnect, erratic supply)
checks: Check the control transformer, 2 A fuse and incoming power connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: VFD SHUTDOWN - VFD fault detected. Check belt and for blower overload. Fix source of fault and reset.
likelyCauses: VFD tripped (overcurrent, overload, DC bus, overtemperature)
Seized blower bearing, belt, or motor fault
checks: Read the fault code on the VFD keypad
Check belt, bearings and motor amps; reset the VFD after repair
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: VFD BYPASS ENGAGED - VFD bypass mode is engaged. Blower may or may not be on. Disengage at MSAV menu.
likelyCauses: Bypass selected in the MSAV (VFD) menu, or bypass contactor engaged
checks: Disengage bypass from the MSAV menu once the VFD is repaired
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW OUTSIDE AIR DAMPER/ECON MECHANICAL FAULT - Damper feedback voltage not within +/- 0.15 V (+/- 2%) of the target within the predefined time.
likelyCauses: Damper actuator failed, binding linkage, or feedback wiring open
Damper blades obstructed / seized
checks: Command the damper in Service > Test and watch the 2-10 V feedback
Check actuator power, control and feedback wiring, and linkage
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Damper Diagnostics' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65
faultCodes.notes: 'Advanced Airflow' on the user interface means Smart Airflow.

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW LOW OUTDOOR AIRFLOW - Actual outdoor air less than target by the percentage set by parameter 239 (default 25%) for the time set by parameter 243 (default 1800 s).
likelyCauses: Blocked outdoor air hood / filters, damper not opening fully
Damper pressure sensor PT5 or supply CFM measurement error
checks: Check outdoor-air hood, filters and damper travel
Check PT5 tubing and sensor
Review parameters 239 and 243
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Ventilation Errors' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW OUTDOOR AIRFLOW TOO HIGH - Actual outdoor air greater than target by the percentage set by parameter 240 for the duration set by parameter 244.
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open or over-travelling; leaking damper blades
PT5 measurement error
checks: Check damper closing and blade seals
Check PT5 tubing/sensor; review parameters 240 and 244
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Ventilation Errors' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW DAMPER PRESSURE ERROR - Differential pressure across the damper (PT5) found not legitimate for the period set by parameter 245.
likelyCauses: PT5 pressure transducer or tubing fault (disconnected, kinked, wrong ports)
Damper position feedback inconsistent with measured pressure
checks: Check PT5 tubing to both sides of the damper and the transducer output
Verify damper feedback and blade condition
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Damper Diagnostics' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: CAI PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK CLOSED - GV1 - Set if S18 is not proved open while the combustion air blower is not energized (open-proof check).
likelyCauses: Proof switch S18 contacts welded / stuck closed
Switch wiring shorted
Inducer still spinning or draft holding the switch closed
checks: With the inducer off, verify S18 contacts are open
Replace S18 if stuck; check wiring for shorts
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Combustion Air Inducer Proof Switch (S18 and S45)' (ManualsLib 1593305 p.18) and Table 65

diagnosticTips: Alarms and events are listed in the Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65/66 (Alarm and Event Codes); alarms marked with * close the service relay DO1. Prodigy (M2) uses Application Guide 506457.

Lockouts ('STRIKE 3 ...' alarms) are cleared from the Service menu (Service > Lockouts / clear lockouts) after the fault is corrected; the number of strikes defaults to 3 (parameter 43 for blower; parameter 98 for high pressure/high temp, 99 for low pressure, 81 for freeze-stat). Even if an alternate occurrence count is set, the alarm text still says 'STRIKE 3'.
Use the LennoxPros 'Error Code Lookup' tool (Technical Tools on LennoxPros.com or the LennoxPros app) to look up any Prodigy alarm number with troubleshooting steps.
Lennox Commercial Technical Support: 800-453-6669 (800-4-LENNOX), 9am-6pm CT; National Accounts 800-367-6285, 8am-5pm CT (lennox.com/commercial/connect).

The M3 has an LCD with menu buttons on the controller face (unit control box). Active alarms take over the screen; press BACK to dismiss the full-screen alarm - the condition still exists and up to two alarm codes stay displayed along the right side of the screen above the thermostat-demand status.

Alarm history: error codes are stored and can be recalled later from the Alarms menu (Settings/Service); the Prodigy M2 Installation & Setup Guide covers viewing and silencing alarms via the user interface.

Test mode: SERVICE > TEST lets you run individual outputs (blower, compressors, heat, damper, exhaust); press SELECT to disable the active test when done. The heartbeat LED is steady green while in test/configuration mode.
Alarms marked with * in Table 65 close the service relay output DO1 (service alarm output) when configured.

Phase/voltage detection (Config ID 2, position 5): N = not installed, 1 = internal Lennox detection, 2/3 = external A42 phase monitor on DI-2 / DI-3. Wrong DI-2 configuration with detection enabled on three-phase units causes demand hold and a 3-minute restart.

Coverage note: Table 65 rows not yet captured: 3, 7, 9-11, 21, 31, 46-49, 80, 87-92, 94-100, 131-135, 138, 140-142, 144-165, 170-177, 186, 190+ (reserved on the M3: 70-72, 84, 104-105, 112-119, 127, 178-181). Rows 17, 18, 19, 54 and 55 have display text reconstructed from the row pattern (evidence single_secondary); rows 40 and 60 were confirmed. The guide states events 12-19 are the high-pressure/high-temperature events.

controls.name: Lennox CORE Control System (M4 unit controller) and CORE Lite
controls.description: Current Lennox unit controller (M4) on Model L (LGM/LCM), Enlight, late Energence and other rooftops, with a four-character seven-segment LED on the board, an optional display and the CORE Service App; CORE Lite is the reduced version on Xion. Numeric alarm codes with a display message and an event action (cause + solution) are listed in the CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (also Setup Guide 508111-01 p.37+). Coverage is partial. Codes with evidence 'manufacturer_doc' were seen in a CORE (M4) document excerpt; codes with 'single_secondary'/'multi_secondary' were copied from the Prodigy 2.0 (M3) Table 65 transcription, which uses the same alarm numbering CORE inherits (spot-checked identical for 1, 4, 5, 13-15, 22-23, 42-43, 82-83, 85) - verify those against Table 11 before relying on them. Alarms captured by message but not by number (ADD ON BOARD PROBLEM, OAC ERROR, No 24VAC relay power A61/TB34-1, RT6/RT17 sensor alarms) are entered with the display text as the code. Expected by pattern but unconfirmed: 16/17 (S28 comp 3), 18/19 (S96 comp 4; 'HIGH PRESS S96 OPEN COMP4' seen without its number), 25, 26-29, 30-37, 45-56 and 121-126. CORE Lite (508676-01) uses the same numbering for the functions it supports.

faultCodes.meaning: ERRATIC POWER (single phase units) - power loss for two cycles; unit power may be dirty or of low quality. Check power connections.
likelyCauses: Loose or corroded line/control power connections
Utility voltage sags, generator or poor power quality
checks: Check and tighten power connections at the disconnect, contactor and controller (manual)
Measure supply voltage under load and compare to nameplate range (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: Strike3 High Press S4 Open Comp - compressor 1 locked out after three high-pressure switch (S4) trips. Event action: check charge, fans and coil; use the Service menu to clear lockouts. (* service relay closes)
likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil
Outdoor (condenser) fan not running: motor, capacitor, contactor or fan relay
Overcharge or non-condensables in the system
Failed, weak or miswired high-pressure switch
checks: Compare head pressure with outdoor ambient (condenser split) and check subcooling (field practice)
Verify condenser fan operation and amps (field practice)
Inspect and clean the condenser coil (manual: check charge, fans, coil)
Check switch continuity and trip point; verify wiring to the controller (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: SMOKE - A173 (smoke detector) input is sensed as closed. Automatically clears once the input is detected open. Event action: check for source of smoke. (* service relay closes)
likelyCauses: Smoke detector A173 tripped (smoke in supply/return air)
Dirty or failed smoke detector head
Wiring/jumper problem on the smoke input
checks: Check for source of smoke (manual)
Inspect and clean/test the duct smoke detector; verify sensitivity and reset it (field practice)
Verify wiring and jumper on the A173 input at the controller (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER - unit off because the air flow switch (S52, normally closed) was detected open after a 16-second delay from blower start. All compressors are de-energized, gas valves closed, electric heat turned off, economizer damper closed and blower stopped. (* service relay closes)

Air flow proving switch S52 tubing, adjustment or failure
Blocked filters/dampers causing insufficient airflow
checks: Verify blower actually runs on a demand (belt, motor, VFD, contactor) (field practice)
Check S52 airflow switch tubing, setpoint and contacts (field practice)
Check filters and damper positions (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

The controller clears the high-pressure alarm when the switch is detected closed; the compressor is not restarted until the switch is closed and the Minimum Off Delay has expired.

Overcharge or non-condensables in the system
Failed, weak or miswired high-pressure switch
checks: Compare head pressure with outdoor ambient (condenser split) and check subcooling (field practice)
Verify condenser fan operation and amps (field practice)

Check switch continuity and trip point; verify wiring to the controller (field practice)

likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil
Outdoor (condenser) fan not running: motor, capacitor, contactor or fan relay
Overcharge or non-condensables in the system

checks: Compare head pressure with outdoor ambient (condenser split) and check subcooling (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 1 LOW PRESS S87 - compressor 1 off: de-energized because low-pressure switch S87 opened (after the low-pressure ignore period). Event action: check charge, filters, airflow and coil.

Dirty filters, iced evaporator or restricted airflow
Restricted metering device / liquid line
Failed or miswired low-pressure switch

Dirty filters, iced evaporator or restricted airflow
Restricted metering device / liquid line
Failed or miswired low-pressure switch
checks: Check charge - superheat and suction pressure vs. evaporator load (manual: check charge, filters, airflow, coil)

faultCodes.meaning: COMP 2 LOW PRESS S88 - compressor 2 de-energized because low-pressure switch S88 opened. Event action: check charge, filters, airflow and coil.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge or leak
Dirty filters, iced evaporator or restricted airflow
Restricted metering device / liquid line

checks: Check charge - superheat and suction pressure vs. evaporator load (manual: check charge, filters, airflow, coil)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR OVERLOAD - alarm set when the blower overload relay switch S42 is detected open; automatically clears once S42 is detected closed. Event action: check external motor overloads.
likelyCauses: Blower motor overload relay S42 tripped (high amps, single-phasing, bad bearings, belt too tight)
Overload relay set too low or failed
Wiring problem on the S42 input
checks: Check the external motor overload (S42) setting and reset it (manual)
Measure blower motor amps on all three phases against FLA (field practice)
Check belt tension, bearings and motor voltage balance (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE3 UNIT SHUTDOWN S42 OR S135 - a motor overload (blower S42 or S135) has occurred multiple times; unit shut down. Event action: check external motor overloads. (* service relay closes)
likelyCauses: Repeated blower/fan motor overload trips (mechanical load, low voltage, phase imbalance)
Failing motor or overload relay
checks: Check external motor overloads S42/S135 and their trip settings (manual)
Measure motor amps and voltage balance; check bearings and belts (field practice)
Clear the lockout from the Service menu after repair (manual)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: NETWORK SENSOR - the network (zone temperature) sensor measurement is out of range; the controller ignores the zone temperature sensor readings and sets the alarm.
likelyCauses: Zone/network sensor open, shorted or disconnected
Wrong sensor type or configuration
Wiring fault on the sensor bus
checks: Check the zone sensor and its wiring (manual)
Verify the sensor is configured for the installed type and the reading is within range (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROLLER RESET - the controller has reset. The reason for the reset will be indicated if known.
likelyCauses: Power interruption or brown-out
Firmware update or manual reset
Internal controller fault
checks: Check the reset reason shown with the alarm (manual)
Check control power and connections; review other alarms logged at the same time (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: INCORRECT SETTINGS - problem with system configuration (model number, Configuration ID 1 and ID 2). If the model number requires a daughter card and it is not detected, this alarm is set. Can only be cleared by resetting or power-cycling the controller. (* service relay closes)
likelyCauses: Model number / Configuration ID 1 or ID 2 entered incorrectly after a board replacement
Required daughter (add-on) board missing or not communicating
checks: Verify model number and Configuration ID 1/ID 2 against the unit nameplate and configuration label (manual)
Verify the required add-on board is installed and seated (manual)
Reset or power-cycle the controller to clear (manual)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: NO DISPLAY - the display is not connected or communication with it is lost.
likelyCauses: Display cable unplugged or damaged
Display board failure
Controller communication port problem
checks: Check the display cable/connector at the controller and display (field practice)
Power-cycle and confirm the display re-establishes communication (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 / CORE Application Guide 485115, Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (seen via search excerpt of the CORE setup manual)

faultCodes.meaning: Advanced Airflow Outside Air Damper / ECON Mechanical Fault - when the damper control voltage is changed and the actuator feedback voltage (P262 DPOS) does not reach the control voltage +/-0.15 V (+/-2 %) within the predefined time, the alarm is triggered (stuck damper / actuator feedback mismatch).
likelyCauses: Economizer damper mechanically stuck, linkage binding or ice
Actuator failure or loss of 24 V
Feedback (DPOS) wire broken or miswired at P262
checks: Command the damper from the Service/test menu and watch travel and feedback voltage (2-10 V = 0-100 %) (manual)
Inspect damper blades, linkage and actuator coupling (field practice)
Check wiring of VOT (control) and DPOS (feedback) at P262 (manual)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Control System Information Guide 508111-03 / Application Guide 485115, damper diagnostics section

faultCodes.meaning: ADD ON BOARD PROBLEM - logged when the CORE Unit Controller is not able to communicate with any attached add-on boards (C3 and GP3). The controller retries communication once every 5 seconds; the alarm automatically clears once communication is restored. (Alarm numbers 79/80 in the M-series table.)
likelyCauses: Add-on (expansion) board unplugged, loose ribbon/expansion connector
Add-on board without power or failed
Wrong configuration calling for a board that is not installed
checks: Check the expansion connector and seating of the C3/GP3 add-on board (manual)
Verify board power LED and communication after re-seating; power-cycle if needed (field practice)
Confirm the configuration ID matches the installed boards (manual)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 Table 11 (manualslib page 41 excerpt)
faultCodes.notes: Alarm number not captured in the CORE excerpt; the Prodigy M2/M3 tables list 79 'ADD-ON BOARD PROBLEM, RESET TO CLEAR' and 80 'ADD-ON BOARD PROBLEM'.

faultCodes.meaning: OAC ERROR - the outdoor-air CFM sensor (A24) input signal is continuously above 25 % of the sensor measuring range for more than five minutes with the blower stopped. The controller disables Outdoor Air CFM control; the alarm automatically clears when the sensor reading is below 10 % of the measuring range for one minute. Event action: check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: A24 outdoor-air CFM (airflow measurement) sensor drifted, dirty or failed
Sensor tubing/wiring problem
Air leaking past the damper with the blower off
checks: Check the A24 sensor and its wiring (manual)
Verify the sensor reads near zero with the blower off and dampers closed (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 Table 11 (manualslib pages 41-42 excerpt)
faultCodes.notes: Alarm number not captured in the excerpt.

faultCodes.meaning: No 24 VAC relay power on the A61 (HP1) board, TB34-1 input - the third and fourth compressors are off. Automatically clears once 24 VAC is present; the controller resumes operation once the ERROR TIME OFF DELAY is completed.
likelyCauses: Blown fuse or open circuit feeding TB34-1 on the A61 board
Safety device in the 24 V relay-power circuit open
Loose connector on the A61 board
checks: Measure 24 VAC at TB34-1 on the A61 (HP1) board (manual)
Trace the 24 V feed to TB34-1 for open fuses, switches or connectors (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 Table 11 (manualslib page 40 excerpt)
faultCodes.notes: Alarm number not captured in the excerpt.

faultCodes.meaning: Discharge air temperature sensor RT6 measurement out of specified range (including open/short detection); the alarm activates and automatically clears once an in-range condition is detected. Event action: check sensor and wiring. (Alarm 77 in the M-series table.)
likelyCauses: RT6 thermistor open or shorted
Wiring/connector fault
Sensor mislocated or damaged

diagnosticTips: Alarm codes are shown on the CORE display with a message and an event action; the full list with cause/solution is Table 11 of the CORE Application Guide 485115 (and the CORE Lite guide 508676-01). Model L specifics are in the CORE Information Guide 508111-03.
Initial configuration, test/service modes and network setup are in the CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01.

Local interface: the M4 CORE board has a four-character seven-segment LED that shows status codes by display priority (see ledPatterns, from the CORE Application Guide 485115 'Local Interface - Four Character Seven-Segment LED' table) and active alarm numbers; full alarm text, time of occurrence and troubleshooting text are shown in the CORE Service App (Bluetooth mobile app, 'Alarms' section) and on the optional display. Alarm history and logs can also be pulled through the USB port.

Alarm numbers, display messages and event actions (cause + solution) are Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' in the CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 (page 37 onward) and section 26.3 of the Application Guide 485115; the CORE Lite equivalent is section 19.3 of guide 508676-01.

Alarms marked * in Table 11 close the service relay contacts (DO1). The contacts stay closed until the controller resets, or the alarm condition clears and the alarm status is read via an explicit S-BUS command.

Compressor strike-3 lockouts (high pressure, low pressure, freezestat) are cleared from the Service menu after correcting the fault. Alarm 83 INCORRECT SETTINGS clears only by resetting or power-cycling the controller.

High-pressure alarms clear when the switch is detected closed; the compressor will not restart until the switch is closed and the Minimum Off Delay has expired. Low-pressure switches are shunted/ignored for 120 s (default, 0-600 s) after a demand; three trips within a demand lock the stage out.
Freezestats S49/S50/S53/S95 (compressors 1-4) are auto-reset: open at 29 F +/-3 on a fall, close at 58 F +/-4 on a rise; three openings lock the compressor out.
Air-flow proving switch S52 must close within 16 s of blower start or alarm 5 shuts the unit down; dirty-filter switch S27 only logs an alarm and can drive the service relay.

Phase/voltage detection: alarms 122-125 are auto-resetting and operation is restored five minutes after proper voltage returns; alarms 121 and 126 require removing power and correcting the problem before service is restored.
Economizer damper diagnostics use the actuator feedback voltage at P262 (DPOS, 2-10 V = 0-100 %); a feedback mismatch of more than +/-0.15 V after the allowed travel time raises alarm 136.
The LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool (LennoxPros.com) covers CORE/M4 alarm numbers with troubleshooting steps.

controls.name: Lennox IMC (Integrated Modular Control) M1-x unit controller
controls.description: Board-mounted microprocessor controller (A55, versions M1-4 through M1-8) on L Series and S-Class (Strategos) gas/electric, electric/electric and heat pump rooftops (c. 1997-2012). Error codes are shown on a 3-digit LED readout on the A55 board (it shows 8.8.8 at power-up) and stored for recall through the pushbutton and MODE DIP switches; configured by DIP switches and ECTO parameters; optional IMC BACnet module and L Connection network. Codes 1-127 were transcribed from the M1-7 Version 5.02 manual Table 4 'IMC Error Codes' via search-engine excerpts of the manualzz text index and the lennoxeurope PDF; the M1-8 Version 6 door label uses the same numbering (codes 1-127). Coverage is partial only because codes 103 and 105 could not be captured cleanly (search excerpts conflated them with 104 and 107) and the gap numbers 7-9, 30-31, 42-43, 70-72 and 111-126 (believed reserved) were not seen verbatim, so they are not listed.

diagnosticTips: Error codes are shown on the A55 IMC board's 3-digit LED readout and stored for later recall (IMC manual Table 4 and Figure 16 list every code; M1-7 v5.02 is at webmanuals.lennoxeurope.com / manualzz 'IMC V7').
The IMC shunts the low-pressure switches (S87/S88) during compressor start until pressure stabilizes, so a low-pressure trip logged after the delay is a real refrigerant/airflow problem.

Where to look: the A55 (M1-7/M1-8) board in the unit control box carries a multi-digit LED readout, a single pushbutton, a green heartbeat LED and MODE DIP switches (UNIT TEST, RECALL, ECTO, TEMP, OPT2, SHIFT). Active error codes are shown on the readout; every code is also stored for recall.

Read stored codes: set the MODE DIP RECALL switch ON, then short-push the pushbutton; stored codes display in reverse order (most recent first) with each short push. A zero means nothing is stored. Set RECALL back OFF when done.
Clear stored codes: with RECALL ON, hold the pushbutton down until 0 is displayed, then turn RECALL OFF.

Reset a lockout: two successive short pushes of the pushbutton reset counters, lockout conditions and timers (codes marked "locked off/locked out" - 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 33, 35, 37, 39, 51, 53, 55, 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 109). A control power reset does the same. Fix the root cause first; manual-reset rollout switches (S47/S69) must be reset at the switch.
A single push of the pushbutton advances to the next display; a double push returns to the previous display (used in ECTO/TEMP modes).

Unit test: the UNIT TEST DIP switch / "Testing Unit Function" section lets the IMC drive individual outputs (blower, compressors, fans, reversing valve, service relay) to check components; thermostat demands can also be simulated by jumpering TB1-6 to TB1-3 (blower), TB1-18 (Y1), TB1-12 (Y2) or TB1-2 (W1). A short push of the pushbutton skips the current delay timer.
The service output (24 VAC alarm relay) is energized by default on the lockout errors marked with * in Table 4; this is what a BAS or remote light sees.

Trip counters: most "opened 3 (default) times" thresholds are set by ECTO parameters (e.g. 1.12/4.14 high pressure, 1.13/4.15 freezestat, 4.04, 3.04, 3.09); a unit configured with a different count will lock out sooner or later than the table states.
The IMC ignores the low-pressure switches during compressor start-up, so a stored low-pressure code (22-29) reflects a real trip after the delay.

Sensor codes 73-78 and 91-99: RT6/RT16/RT17 are 2-wire thermistors, A2 zone sensors are a 2-wire thermistor with a 1k series resistor; measure resistance at the board terminals against the temperature-resistance chart before replacing.
LennoxPros.com Error Code Lookup tool (Technical Tools) covers IMC codes; Lennox Commercial Technical Support 800-453-6669 (9am-6pm CT).

Another possible cause is electrical noise interference affecting the communicating system when the compressor contactor coil is energized. Corrective Action:
Communicating system: Wire a transient voltage suppressor in parallel with the compressor contactor coil terminals on the outdoor unit.

Non-communicating outdoor unit: Wire transient voltage suppressor (89W72) in parallel with compressor contactor coil or across the Y1 and C terminals on the indoor unit control. NOTE: See service and application note IAQ-10-01 for further details. Transient Voltage Suppressor Part information: Made by Little Fuse, part number 5KP43CA bidirectional Transorb aka TVS Diode. Please contact your FTC or inside technical support for help in acquiring the transient voltage suppressor if not available in your local electronics store.

Outdoor Unit and Zoning When the heat pump could not get a zone thermostat to progress 0.5°F towards the set point in 30 minutes the system will lock out the heat pump and switch to the secondary heat source. Electric heat or if in dual-fuel applications the furnace will be used and the system put in heat pump heating lockout timer) default is 120 minutes. It will lock the heat pump off and the gas furnace will finish the heating cycle Set the low balance point and high balance point as close together as possible. (This is a 3°F difference – Example: set high balance point at 25°F and low balance point would set at 22°F). faultCodes.meaning: Wiring Issue / Communication Problem: Low voltage wiring between one of the systems components has been compromised. The System component (device) is unable to communicate.
checks: S30 - Access Dealer Control Center - Select notification icon, review alert code details to determine which device or unit's low voltage wiring is experiencing a communication issue. Review both active and cleared alerts.

Wi-Fi - Press and hold the Lennox logo on bottom right of stat for 5 seconds to access the dealer control center. Follow prompts to access the “Alerts” tab. Review alert code details to determine which device or unit's low voltage wiring is experiencing a communication issue, Review both active and cleared alerts. Troubleshooting: Step 1 In most cases, issues can be resolved by taking the following actions:

Confirm all unused wires are tied together and taken back to the “C” terminal on the indoor board as shown in the installation and setup guide. See “Figure 5. Minimizing Electrical Noise (S40)” on page 5 for illustration on bundling unused wires to common.
Check for loose terminal connections on components (devices). Lennox recommends using a slotted screwdriver with a 3/32” (2.4 mm) tip.
Check for incorrectly wired or poorly spliced connections between components.
Verify that low voltage going to system components has been separated from high voltage wiring in wall, ceiling, & floor cavities.

Check for proper grounding on the line voltage and low voltage wiring, transformer, and equipment. If 105 Alert Code is still present after performing the actions listed above proceed to Troubleshoot- ing: Step 2. Troubleshooting: Step 2

Disconnect all wiring to other components (except S30 thermostat to Smart Hub, Smart Hub to indoor unit) and reconnect one device at a time. Recommission system each time a device is added until wiring issue has been located.

Zoning: If a zoning system has been installed and is wired directly from the thermostat to the zoning control then disconnect wiring and run control wiring from the zoning control directly to the indoor unit control. Wiring diagrams are provided in the LZSV Zoning System installation and Setup guide.
Float Switch: When using a float switch, use an isolation relay between the dedicated float switch terminals. For testing purposes, remove float switch from circuit.

Check for Inductive voltage from surrounding sources. Check each wire in AC mode to “C” on circuit board. > An inductive voltage of 0.3 - 0.3 VAC in not an issue. > An inductive voltage of up to 0.7 VACs can provide a moderate success rate. > An inductive voltage up to 1.2 VACs can provide an occasional success rate. > Any inductive voltage over 1.2 VAC needs to be addressed. If 105 Alert Code is still present after performing the actions listed above proceed to troubleshoot- ing Step 3. Troubleshooting: Step 3 New low voltage wiring will need to be ran to the system components. There are two options for replacing low voltage wiring: 1. Utilizing 18/2 AWG for wires going to 24VAC (R & C) terminals and 18-22/2 AWG shielded wires going communicating terminals(i+ & i-); Utilizing 18/2 AWG for wires going to 12V (+12V & -12V) terminals and 18-22/2 AWG shielded wires going communicating terminals (A& B). Wiring diagrams are provided in the installation manual. 2. Utilizing 2 separate 18/2 AWG unshielded wires. One set wire to 24VAC terminals (R & C) and one set to communicating terminals (i+ & i-); Utilizing 2 separate 18/2 AWG unshielded wires. One set wire to 12V terminals (+12V & -12V) and one set to communicating terminals (A & B). Wiring diagrams provided in the installation manual. See “1.1. Communication Wiring Options” on page 2 for wiring diagrams.

faultCodes.meaning: AC Line Frequency / Distortion Prob: In most cases the errors will have something to do with the transformer(s) phasing, input power or output loading (amperage load). For the air handler control only, alert code 114 is generated only if the measured line frequency is below 57Hz or above 63Hz and remains out of range for 10 consecutive seconds. We count power line cycles and determine line frequency every one second of time based on the proces- sor's quartz crystal oscillator. We have a fair amount of filtering on when we consider a power line cycle to have occurred, so there would have to be really bad distortion for it to count an extra cycle or miss a real cycle. Voltage low enough to miss a cycle would generate an alert code 115. There are lots of events, such as power utility substation switching, that could occasionally make our power line frequency off by one count. These are rare one-time events and I don't know anything other than a generator with bad frequency that could cause problems long enough to cause this alert code. There is a frequency / distortion problem with the power to a specific system component. This alert code may indicate transformer overload- ing.
checks: Check the voltage and line power frequency.
Check the generator operating frequency, if the system is running on back-up power.
Correct voltage and frequency problems.
System will resume normal operation five seconds after fault recovered.
All applicable system component outputs are disabled – service soon condition.
After 10 minutes, the priority condition is escalated – service critical condition.
Damper control module will operate in central mode only until the proper voltage is restored or frequency distortion is resolved.

If connected to Lennox Smart Zoning, set damper control module transformer jumper to system transformer. Check for proper wiring. Replace 40VAC furnace transformer with 70VAC transformer. Re-commission system. NOTE: The unitary control (outdoor unit control board) whether it is a single, two-stage or multi-stage control is not displaying alert code 114.
