controls.name: Lennox residential gas furnace integrated control with 7-segment display (SL280UHV, SL280UHNV / SL280UHNVK, EL296UHV)
controls.description: Two-stage / variable-speed Lennox furnace controls show status letters and E-codes on a 7-segment display. E-code numbers equal the communicating alert codes (E223 = alert 223, see platform lennox-icomfort-alerts). K-suffix (refrigerant-detection-ready) furnaces add A2L codes E150-E164 and E390.

faultCodes.meaning: No error in memory
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39

faultCodes.meaning: Device communication problem - No other devices on RS BUS (Communication system).
checks: Equipment is unable to communicate.
Indicates numerous message errors.
In most cases errors are related to electrical noise.
Make sure high voltage power is separated from RSBus.
Check for miswired and/or loose connections between the stat, indoor unit and outdoor unit.
Check for a high voltage source of noise close to the system.
Fault clears after communication is restored.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 105 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low line voltage.
checks: Line Voltage Low (Voltage lower than nameplate rating).
Check power line voltage and correct.
Alarm clears 5 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 110 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low line voltage.
checks: Reverse line power voltage wiring.
System resumes normal operation 5 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 111 (Alert Code Guide 100017). The manual's diagnostic text reads 'Low line voltage' but the action and Alert Code Guide 100017 (alert 111 'GF Line Polarity Reversed') describe reversed line polarity.

faultCodes.meaning: Ground not detected
checks: System shuts down.
Provide proper earth ground.
System resumes normal operation 5 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 112 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: High line voltage.
checks: Line Voltage High (Voltage higher than nameplate rating).
Provide power voltage within proper range.
System resumes normal operation 5 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 113 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Line voltage frequency out-of-range.
checks: No 60 Hertz Power.
Check voltage and line power frequency.
Correct voltage and frequency problems.
System resumes normal operation 5 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 114 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low 24V - Control will restart if the error recovers.
checks: 24-Volt Power Low (Range is 18 to 30 volts).
Check and correct voltage.
Check for additional power-robbing equipment connected to system.
May require installation of larger VA transformer to be installed in furnace / air handler.
Clears after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 115 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Poor ground detected (Warning only)
checks: Provide proper grounding for unit.
Check for proper earth ground to the system.
Warning only will clear 30 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 117 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Unresponsive device. Communication only.
checks: Usually caused by delay in outdoor unit responding to indoor unit poling.
Recycle power.
Check all wiring connections.
Cleared after unresponsive device responds to any inquiry.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 120 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Active communicating thermostat signal missing for more than 3 minutes.
checks: Equipment lost communication with the thermostat.
Check four wiring connections, ohm wires and cycle power at the thermostat.
Alert stops all services and waits for heartbeat message from thermostat (subnet controller).
Cleared after valid thermostat (subnet controller) message is received.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 124 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Control failed self-check, internal error, failed hardware. Will restart if error recovers. Integrated control not communicating. Covers hardware errors (flame sense circuit faults, pin shorts, etc.).
checks: Hardware problem on the control.
Cycle power on control.
Replace if problem prevents service and is persistent.
Critical alert.
Cleared 300 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 125 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Corrupted control parameters (Verify configuration of system). Communicating only.
checks: Reconfigure the system.
Replace control if heating or cooling is not available.
Only applicable in the communicating mode, not in startup.
Exit from Commissioning and Execute 'Set Factory Default' mode.
Control will still operate on default parameter settings.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39

faultCodes.meaning: A2L Refrigerant leak alarm
checks: This may indicate the presence of a leak at or in the indoor unit coil of the equipment, that will need to be repaired for proper and safe operation.
Additionally, it may indicate that proper refrigerant charge will need to be verified.
The fault cannot be cleared while the refrigerant detection system sensor is reporting the presence of a leak.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector Sensor #1 fault
checks: The refrigerant detection sensor #1 in the unit is reporting an issue that prevents it from functioning properly and replacement of the sensor may be necessary.
This fault clears when the sensor no longer reports the presence of a fault condition.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector #2 Fault
checks: The refrigerant detection sensor #1 [sic, sensor #2] in the unit is reporting an issue that prevents it from functioning properly and replacement of the sensor may be necessary.
This fault clears when the sensor no longer reports the presence of a fault condition.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces. The manual text says 'sensor #1' here; it applies to sensor #2.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector #1 Communication lost or invalid sensor dip switch configuration (ON/OFF)
checks: There may be an issue with the wiring harness connecting the sensor #1 to the furnace control board, either with the wiring itself or with the connector.
Check the wiring and connector for damage or improper connectivity.
Check the sensor for damage or obstruction on the harness plug.
This fault clears when communications with the sensor has been reestablished, but blower latches for a minimum 5 minutes.
Retest of the presence of fault can be effected by pressing the LOW GWP test button on the furnace unit control board.
This may also indicate incorrect LOW GWP dip switch settings.
See installation instructions.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector #2 Communication lost
checks: There may be an issue with the wiring harness connecting the sensor #1 [sic, sensor #2] to the furnace control board, either with the wiring itself or with the connector.
Check the wiring and connector for damage or improper connectivity.
Check the sensor for damage or obstruction on the harness plug.
This fault clears when communications with the sensor has been reestablished, but blower latches for a minimum 5 minutes.
Retest of the presence of fault can be effected by pressing the LOW GWP test button on the furnace unit control board.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces. The manual text says 'sensor #1' here; it applies to sensor #2.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector Sensor #1 type incorrect
checks: The sensor #1 is of a type not suitable for use in the application.
Replace the sensor with a Lennox approved replacement part.
This fault clears when a sensor suitable for the application is detected by the furnace control board, but blower will latch for a minimum of 5 minutes.
Retest of the presence of the fault can be effected by pressing the LOW GWP test button on the furnace unit control board.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant Leak Detector Sensor #2 type incorrect
checks: The sensor #2 is of a type not suitable for use in the application.
Replace the sensor with a Lennox approved replacement part.
This fault clears when a sensor suitable for the application is detected by the furnace control board, but blower will latch for a minimum of 5 minutes.
Retest of the presence of the fault can be effected by pressing the LOW GWP test button on the furnace unit control board.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Furnace Control Board Failure
checks: There is an issue with the furnace control board, preventing the furnace from operating properly.
This may require the replacement of the indoor unit control board.
This fault clears when the furnace controller operates normally.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Low GWP Test
checks: Low GWP Test mode activates by manually engaging Low GWP test button.
Normal operations resumes and codes clear automatically after 1-minute.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Refrigerant-detection (A2L / R-454B) code on K-suffix refrigerant-detection-ready furnaces.

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor air temperature sensor failure. Only shown if shorted or out-of range.
checks: Compare outdoor sensor resistance to temperature/resistance charts in unit installation instructions.
Replace sensor pack if necessary.
At beginning of (any) configuration, furnace or air handler control will sense outdoor air and discharge air temperature sensor(s).
If detected (reading in range), appropriate feature will be set as 'installed' and that could be seen in 'About' screen.
In normal operation after control recognizes sensors, alarm will be sent if valid temperature reading is lost.
To get rid of setting and alarm, redo configuration and make sure that temperature sensor is marked as 'not installed' in Indoor Unit 'About' screen.
When Indoor unit control is replaced, thermostat will 'tell' new control if temperature sensor is in system or not.
Clears 30 seconds after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 180 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Hard lockout - Rollout circuit open or previously open.
checks: Correct cause of rollout trip, or replace flame rollout switch.
Test furnace operation.
Cleared after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 200 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor blower communication failure - Unable to communicate with blower motor.
checks: Indoor blower communication failure (including power outage).
Lost communication with indoor blower motor.
Possible causes: motor not powered, loose wiring.
Problem may be on control or motor side.
Cleared after fault recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 201 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor blower motor mis-match - Indoor motor horsepower does not match unit capacity.
checks: Incorrect appliance capacity code selected.
Check for proper configuring under: Unit Size Codes for Furnace/Air Handler on configuration guide or in installation instructions.
Cleared after the correct match is detected following a reset.
(Remove thermostat from system while applying power and reprogramming.)
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 202 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Appliance capacity / size is NOT programmed. Invalid unit codes refer to configuration flow chart.
checks: No appliance capacity code selected.
Check for proper configuring under: Unit Size Codes for Furnace on configuration guide or in installation instructions.
Critical Alert.
Cleared after valid unit code is read following a reset.
(Remove thermostat from system while applying power and reprogramming.)
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 203 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Gas valve mis-wired.
checks: Check gas valve operation and wiring.
Clears when repaired.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 204 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Gas valve control relay contact shorted.
checks: Check wiring on control and gas valve.
If wiring is correct, replace control.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 205 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Gas valve second-stage relay failure
checks: Furnace will operate on 1st stage for remainder of the heating demand.
Will clear after fault recovered.
If unable to operate 2nd stage, replace control.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 206 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Hot surface ignitor sensed open.
checks: Measure resistance of hot surface ignitor.
Replace if open or not within specified range found in IOM.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 207 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure switch failed open.
checks: Check pressure (inches w.c.) of low pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 223 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure switch failed closed.
checks: Check operation of low pressure switch to see if it is stuck closed on heat call longer than 150 seconds.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 224 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure switch failed open.
checks: Check pressure (inches w.c.) of high pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 225 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure switch failed closed
checks: Check operation of high pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 226 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure switch open during trial for ignition or run mode.
checks: Check pressure (inches w.c.) of low pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 227 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Combustion air inducer calibration failure
checks: Unable to perform pressure switch calibration.
Check vent system and pressure switch wiring connections.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 228 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Ignition on high fire
checks: IFC switched to high fire ignition because low fire pressure switch did not close in allowed time.
No action is needed.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 229 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Low flame current - Run mode.
checks: Check micro-amperes of flame sensor using control diagnostics or field-installed mode.
Clean or replace sensor.
Measure voltage of neutral to ground to ensure good unit ground.
Alert clears after current heat call has been completed.
See TABLE 26.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 240 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Flame sensed out of sequence - Flame still present.
checks: Shut off gas.
Check for gas valve leak.
Replace, if necessary.
Alert clears when fault is recovered.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 241 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Limit switch circuit open.
checks: Check for proper firing rate on furnace.
Ensure there is no blockage in heater.
Check for proper air flow.
If limit not closed within 3 minutes, unit will go into 1-hour soft lockout.
Resumes normal operation after fault is cleared.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 250 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Discharge air temperature too high (gas heat only).
checks: Check temperature rise, air flow and input rate.
Cleared when heat call is finished.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 252 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Exceeded maximum number of retries. No flame current sensed.
checks: Check for proper gas flow.
Ensure that ignitor is lighting burner.
Check flame sensor current.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 270 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Exceeded maximum number of retries. Last retry failed due to the pressure switch opening.
checks: Check pressure (inches w.c.) of low pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 271 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Exceeded maximum number of recycles. Last recycle due to the pressure switch opening.
checks: Check operation of low pressure switch to see if it is stuck closed on heat call.
Check pressure (inches w.c.) of high pressure switch closing on heat call.
Measure operating pressure (inches w.c.).
Inspect vent and combustion air inducer for correct operation and restriction.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 272 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Exceeded maximum number of recycles. Last recycle due to flame failure.
checks: Check micro-amperes of flame sensor using control diagnostics or field-installed mode.
Clean or replace sensor.
Measure voltage of neutral to ground to ensure good unit ground.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 273 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Exceeded maximum number of recycles. Last recycle failed due to the limit circuit opening or limit remained open longer than 3 minutes
checks: Shut down system. 1-hour soft lockout.
Check firing rate and air flow.
Check for blockage.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 274 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Soft lockout - Flame sensed out of sequence. Flame signal is gone.

faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 275 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 290 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor blower motor unable to start due to obstructed wheel, seized bearings.

faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 292 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor blower motor temperature is too high.

faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 295 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Discharge error temperature sensor failure. Only shown if shorted or out of range.
checks: Compare outdoor sensor resistance to temperature/resistance charts in installation instructions.
Replace sensor if necessary.
Cleared in Communicating mode: 30 seconds after fault recovered.
In Non-Communicating mode: Cleared after the current heat call is completed.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 310 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Heat rate reduced to match indoor blower air flow.
checks: Warning Only.
Furnace blower in cutback mode due to restricted airflow.
Reduce firing rate every 60 seconds to match available CFM.
Check filter and duct system.
To clear, replace filter if needed or repair/add duct. 2-stage controls will reduce firing rate to 1st stage.
Clears when heat call finishes successfully.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 311 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

faultCodes.meaning: Restricted air flow in cooling or continuous fan mode is lower than cfm setting.
checks: Warning Only.

Restricted airflow - Indoor blower is running at a reduced CFM (Cutback Mode - The variable speed motor has pre-set speed and torque limiters to protect the motor from damage caused by operating outside of design parameters (0 to 0.8" W.C. total external static pressure)).
Check filter and duct system.
To clear, replace filter if needed or repair/add duct.
Cleared after the current service demand is satisfied.
faultCodes.source: SL280UHNVK Installation Instructions 508561-01 (04/2026), Ignition Control Diagnostic Codes pp.34-39
faultCodes.notes: Same number as Lennox communicating alert 312 (Alert Code Guide 100017).

safetyDevices: S4 / S7 high pressure switches (auto-reset; controller counts strikes and locks out after three - alarm 13 on IMC/CORE)
S87 / S88 low pressure switches (shunted by A55 during start-up)
S10 primary limit and rollout switches on gas heat sections
S52 blower airflow proving switch (Prodigy 2.0 alarm 5 / STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER)

terminalLabels.R: 24 VAC hot to thermostat (Lennox convention - verify on unit controller)
terminalLabels.DO1: Service relay output (closes on selected alarms; Prodigy 2.0/CORE)

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (unit-controller units): on Y1 (or network demand) A55 energizes the indoor blower (B3) and, after proving airflow via S52, energizes compressor contactor K1 (compressor B1) and the condenser fans (B4/B5 via K68); low-pressure switches S87/S88 are shunted during start-up. Y2 brings on the second compressor/stage (B2). High-pressure switch S4/S7 trips de-energize the compressor; three trips = strike-3 lockout (alarm 13).

Heating (gas): on W1 the ignition control A3 checks limits (S10, rollout) and the combustion-air pressure switch, runs the combustion blower prepurge, energizes the spark/igniter and gas valve GV1, and proves flame; the blower starts after the heat-on delay. W2 adds the second heat stage. Repeated ignition failures produce a heat lockout alarm on the unit controller.

Economizer: the unit controller (A55; economizer board A56 EM1 on IMC units) modulates the outdoor-air damper actuator for free cooling when outdoor conditions are suitable; mechanical cooling is staged behind it. The zone sensor A2 supplies the space temperature.
notes: Confirmed against Lennox documents: A55, K1, S4, S87, S88 (wiring diagram 538043-03 and service literature 100087) and B1, B3, B4/B5, K68, T1/CB8, A2, A3, S10, S52, S42, A42 (Unit Information legend 100074). Designators marked 'named in IMC/Prodigy codes' are taken from the alarm texts transcribed in controls[] (manufacturer documents), not from a legend; check every designator against the legend printed on the unit's wiring diagram (inside the control compartment door). Lennox numbering convention: A = controls/boards, B = motors, K = relays/contactors, S = switches, RT = temperature sensors, T = transformers, CB = circuit breakers, GV = gas valves.
The sequence of operation is generic to Lennox unit-controller rooftops; the model-specific sequence is in the unit's service literature ('Unit Information') and IOM.
Landmark/Raider units without a unit controller use conventional 24 V thermostat wiring through relays and a defrost/ignition board.

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor keeps running / will not shut off during high outdoor humidity on a Prodigy 2.0 unit
likelyCauses: BAS/network dehumidification setpoints set unreasonably low by previous technicians, keeping the compressor on (documented resolution in the cited HVAC-Talk thread 2243831; the Lennox-recommended M3 board swap did not fix it)

Dehumidification (Humiditrol / reheat) or humidity-based control parameter keeping mechanical cooling on when the outdoor humidity sensor reads above the setpoint (reported field pattern, forum-level evidence)
Faulty or mis-scaled outdoor/return humidity sensor
checks: Review the BAS/network dehumidification setpoints before replacing the M3 board
Check the humidity sensor readings on the Prodigy display against a calibrated meter
Review dehumidification settings and disable to confirm the behaviour changes
Check Prodigy firmware level and controller parameters against the setup guide
sources: HVAC-Talk thread 'Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Issue' (hvac-talk.com/threads/lennox-prodigy-2-0-issue.2243831/) - resolved by correcting BAS dehumidification setpoints

commonIssues.symptom: Loss of communication between the Prodigy/M2 controller and the network or display; controller replaced more than once
likelyCauses: Controller (Prodigy M2/M3) board failure
Network wiring / termination faults
Poor power quality (erratic power alarms)
checks: Check 24 VAC supply and grounding at A55
Inspect network daisy-chain wiring, polarity and termination
Verify firmware and replace the controller only after wiring and power are proven
sources: HVAC-Talk threads 'Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Issue' and 'Lennox Prodigy Board'

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor locked out on high pressure (IMC code 13 / CORE alarm 13 Strike3 High Press S4)
likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil
Outdoor fan motor / capacitor failure
Overcharge or non-condensables
Failed S4 switch
checks: Compare head pressure to outdoor ambient (condenser split) and subcooling
Confirm outdoor fan runs and draws normal amps
Clean coil; check S4 trip/reset points
Clear the lockout from the Service menu (CORE/Prodigy) or reset the IMC after repair
sources: Lennox CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 (alarm 13 event action: check charge, fans and coil)

commonIssues.symptom: Nuisance low-pressure trips at compressor start in cold weather
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge or restricted airflow (dirty filters, iced coil) - the A55 controller shunts S87/S88 only during start-up, so trips after the delay are real
Failed low-pressure switch
checks: Verify suction pressure after the start-up shunt period
Check filters, blower operation and evaporator coil
Check S87/S88 continuity and setpoint
sources: Lennox Unit Information service literature 100087 (A55 shunts low pressure switches during start-up)

commonIssues.symptom: Blower alarm / STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER lockout (Prodigy 2.0)
likelyCauses: Broken or slipping blower belt
Blower motor overload or VFD fault
S52 airflow switch or tubing fault
Excessive static (dirty filters, closed dampers)
checks: Inspect belt tension/condition and sheave alignment
Measure blower motor amps vs. FLA; check VFD fault log
Verify S52 switch operation and tubing
Clear the lockout from the UI after repair
sources: Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER)

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not bringing in outdoor air / stuck at minimum or fully open
likelyCauses: Stuck or seized damper / linkage
Failed actuator
Failed or drifted outdoor/return sensors (temperature or enthalpy)
Incorrect changeover settings
checks: Command the damper through the controller's test mode and watch travel
Check actuator power and feedback
Compare sensor readings to a reference thermometer/psychrometer
Review economizer setpoints in the controller
sources: PNNL 'Best Practices for Air-Side Economizers Operation and Maintenance' (stuck dampers, sensor failures, linkages, actuators, settings)
Lennox Economizer for Energence rooftop units instruction (manuals.plus mirror)

support.literatureSearchHint: On LennoxPros.com go to Resources > Document Library and search by the full model number (e.g. LGH120H4BH1G) or serial number; filter by 'Installation Instructions' (IOM), 'Service Literature' (Unit Information, includes wiring legend) or 'Wiring Diagram'. PDFs are hosted at tech.lennoxintl.com and lennox.com/dA/. Engineering handbooks with the model number identification page are named ehb_<family>_*.pdf (e.g. ehb_lgh_cbox_2103.pdf).
support.notes: The LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool (Technical Tools) decodes Prodigy/CORE/IMC alarm numbers with troubleshooting steps.

notes: Nameplate: the factory MODEL NO. and SERIAL NO. are on the unit rating plate on the compressor/control side; the serial is always 10 characters on 1973+ equipment. Catalog numbers such as L1318 or 45W08 are LennoxPros stock numbers, not model numbers.

Lennox rooftop nomenclature (2009+) is positional: brand letter, unit type (G gas/electric, C electric/electric, H heat pump, D dual fuel), generation/family letter, 3-digit nominal cooling MBH, efficiency (S/H/U), refrigerant (4 = R-410A, 5 = R-454B), blower type, heat input (gas S/M/H, N none), minor design digit, voltage (P 208-230/1, Y 208-230/3, G 460/3, J 575/3), then optional factory-installed option codes.

Family names verified: L Series LGA/LCA/LHA (and LGC/LCC), Strategos SGA/SCA + SGB/SCB + SGC/SCC + SGH/SCH, Energence LGH/LCH, Enlight LGT/LCT/LHT/LDT, Model L LGM/LCM, Xion LGX/LCX/LHX (not XGA/XCA), Landmark KGA/KCA/KHA + KGB/KCB/KHB/KDB, Raider ZGA/ZCA/ZHA + ZGB/ZCB/ZHB + ZGD/ZCD, T-Class TSA/TPA/TAA. Lennox lists Model L, Enlight, Xion and Raider as four distinct lines (comparison sheet 37J72). CBA/CBH/CBX are residential air handlers; 'Elite' ELS/ELC could not be verified.

Residual gaps after the verification pass: Prodigy 2.0 Table 65 rows listed as 'not yet captured' in the prodigy coverage note; CORE codes copied from the Prodigy tables are only spot-checked against CORE Table 11 (24, 40, 41 and the 38-132 block are not individually confirmed); IMC codes 103 and 105 were not captured cleanly; the 38Z29 rooftop model number identifier sheet and the L Series EHB model-ID page are still unread (T-Class part-load/coil letters, Landmark/Raider D/E blower letters and the trailing W on single-phase listings remain unconfirmed).
Lennox Commercial Controls System (LCCS) and L Connection Network are BAS/network layers, not unit controllers; alarm codes come from the unit controller (IMC/Prodigy/CORE).

Residential (2026-10-20): added the Lennox communicating alert table (Alert Code Guide 100017, all 207 rows incl. inverter flash cross-reference), furnace 7-segment E-codes (SL280UHNVK 508561-01), SureLight two-stage DS1/DS2 and X+Y tables (Corp. 0222-L7), ML180UHE and ML180UH (2018) red-LED tables, and residential outdoor (EL16XC1/EL16KP1/XP16) and gas furnace (SL280/EL296/ML180) nomenclature. Not covered: iComfort E30/M30-specific guides, legacy iComfort Wi-Fi and ComfortSense 7500 codes, single-stage SureLight boards 56L83/63K89/97L48 and G40/G43/G50/G60/G61 codes, non-communicating outdoor boards (LSOM, 103369 defrost), residential air handler and coil nomenclature.

Research correction: the residential nomenclature notes give 090 = 88,000 Btuh only by analogy; the SL280UHV bulletin (form 210600) confirms 070 = 66,000, 090 = 88,000, 110 = 110,000, 135 = 132,000 Btuh and X = low NOx (40 ng/J), which the furnace format uses.
